title: Lampstand, Bread, and Punishment for Blasphemy

questions.question: What kind of oil was used for the lamps?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:2 (ESV): "Bring you pure oil from beaten olives for the lamp."

questions.question: How many loaves of bread were set in rows?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:5-6 (ESV): "You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves... set them in two piles, six in a pile."

questions.question: Who blasphemed the Name and cursed?
options: A son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father
questions.correctAnswer: A son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:10-11 (ESV): "Now an Israelite woman's son, whose father was an Egyptian... blasphemed the Name and cursed."

questions.question: What was the punishment for blaspheming the name of the Lord?
options: He shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:16 (ESV): "Whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him."

questions.question: What is the rule "eye for eye" known as?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:20 (ESV): "Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth."

questions.question: Where was the man put while awaiting God's decision?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:12 (ESV): "And they put him in custody, till the will of the Lord should be clear to them."

questions.question: Who laid their hands on the blasphemer's head?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:14 (ESV): "Let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him."

questions.question: Does the law for blasphemy apply to strangers?
options: Yes, stranger as well as native
No, they have their own gods
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, stranger as well as native
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:16 (ESV): "The sojourner as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death."

questions.question: What was put on each pile of bread?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:7 (ESV): "And you shall put pure frankincense on each pile."

questions.question: When was the bread arranged before the Lord?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:8 (ESV): "Every Sabbath day Aaron shall arrange it before the Lord regularly."

questions.question: The bread was considered what kind of covenant?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:8 (ESV): "It is from the people of Israel as a covenant forever."

questions.question: What happens to one who kills an animal Vs one who kills a person?
options: One makes restitution, the other is put to death
questions.correctAnswer: One makes restitution, the other is put to death
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:21 (ESV): "Whoever kills an animal shall make it good, and whoever kills a person shall be put to death."

questions.question: The woman's name was Shelomith. Which tribe was she from?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:11 (ESV): "His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan."

questions.question: Where was the lampstand placed?
options: Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting
questions.correctAnswer: Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting
questions.explanation: Leviticus 24:3 (ESV): "Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it."

questions.question: The twelve loaves represented what?
questions.explanation: Implicit symbolism, supported by the context of "from the people of Israel" (v8).

key_verse_text: Whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him. The sojourner as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
